data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 names a specific inherited variable — the isomorphism-revealing confrontation that translation enables — but its refutation condition (a lineage achieving confrontation without translating into a rival vocabulary) does not actually test the inheritance. The condition challenges dependence on translation, but it never tests whether the inherited variable itself is the confrontation as opposed to any other productive output of translation (e.g., vocabulary enrichment, analogy generation). A lineage could satisfy the refutation by achieving isomorphism-revealing confrontation via direct structural comparison without a rival-vocabulary translation, yet this would show only that translation is not the unique route to confrontation; the sharpening claim — that confrontation rather than translation is the operative causal variable — is still not independently falsified. The refutation thus severs dependence but leaves the inheritance assertion untouched: the target conflates refuting a prerequisite with refuting an inherited differentiator.
